title: Global power lifting detects affine algebraic spaces over arbitrary rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. A quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra means a sheaf of commutative unital $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras on the small etale site whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]; surjective means surjective as a sheaf, and $\Gamma(Z,-)$ denotes global sections. Suppose that for every surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of such algebras and every $c\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal C)$, there are an integer $N>0$ and $b\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal B)$ whose image is $c^N$. Then $Z$ is represented by an affine scheme. Neither $R$ nor $Z$ is assumed Noetherian or of finite type.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, Lemma 4.1.8 (3) implies (2), printed pp.502-504, and Theorem 4.3.1, printed pp.505-506. Global power-lifting formulation, with no field hypothesis. Local PDF WANTED; journal version read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: Choose a finite surjective finitely presented scheme cover $p:Y\to Z$. Its source is qcqs by the cited finite-presentation source lemma. Given a surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $Y$, both $p_*\mathcal B$ and $p_*\mathcal C$ are quasi-coherent, by the degree-zero case of the higher-direct-image lemma. This pushforward is still surjective: on every affine etale chart $V\to Z$, the scheme $W=Y\times_ZV$ is affine by finiteness, and affine-chart sections compute cokernels, so $\mathcal B(W)\to\mathcal C(W)$ is surjective. The direct-image chart-limit definition identifies its value on $V$ with sections over $W$: a compatible family on all etale charts of $W$ is exactly a section by the sheaf gluing axiom. The same definition identifies global sections of $p_*\mathcal B$ and $p_*\mathcal C$ with those of $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$. Apply the assumed property on $Z$ to these pushed-forward algebras. Thus $Y$ has the same global positive-power-lifting property.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.1, printed p.506, final paragraph; Tag 09YC, and the affine-chart justification of the sentence that the covering scheme is adequately affine. Local PDF WANTED; journal PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: Use the Zariski-etale quasi-coherent equivalence to work on the scheme $Y$ with Zariski quasi-coherent algebras; restriction preserves global sections and the tensor-pullback description identifies algebra structures. Surjectivity is detected on affine charts, so the lifting property just obtained applies to these algebras. Put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. For a closed point $q\in Y$, choose an affine open $U$ containing $q$. Choose quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I,\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ cutting out $Y\setminus U$ and $\{q\}$, respectively. Their vanishing sets are disjoint, so $\mathcal I+\mathcal J=\mathcal O_Y$: at every stalk one ideal is the unit ideal. Consequently the composite $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J$ is surjective. Its target is quasi-coherent by affine-chart cokernel calculus. The induced map $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J)$ is a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras. Let $t$ be the global degree-one section given by $1$ modulo $\mathcal J$. Power lifting supplies $N>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I))$ mapping to $t^N$.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.1, printed pp.505-506, scheme argument, first displayed symmetric-algebra surjection. We use any ideal of the closed singleton instead of its residue-field skyscraper. Local PDF WANTED; journal PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: Take the degree-$N$ component $s_N$ of $s$. This is a global section: on every affine open the symmetric algebra has its cited direct-sum grading, and the degree projections commute with restrictions, since restrictions send degree-one generators to degree-one generators. The same generator calculation shows that the symmetric-algebra map preserves degrees, hence $s_N$ maps to $t^N$. Evaluate $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)\to\mathcal O_Y$ via the inclusion of $\mathcal I$, and let $f$ be the image of $s_N$. Locally it is a sum of products of $N$ elements of $\mathcal I$, so $f\in\mathcal I^N\subseteq\mathcal I$ since $N>0$. Modulo $\mathcal J$, evaluation agrees with the map $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J)\to\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J$ sending its degree-one section $t$ to $1$, by the symmetric-algebra universal property. Thus $f\equiv1\pmod{\mathcal J}$. Therefore $q\in Y_f\subseteq U$, and $Y_f=D_U(f|_U)$ is affine by the affine principal-open lemma.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.1, printed p.506, construction of f and the equality X_f=U_f. Taking the positive homogeneous component makes the vanishing on the complement explicit. Local PDF WANTED; journal PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: The opens $Y_f$ so obtained cover all closed points, hence all of $Y$. Indeed, the complement of their union is a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $Y$; if nonempty it has a point closed in $Y$ by the cited Kolmogorov-space lemma, contradicting the construction. The underlying space of a scheme is Kolmogorov directly from its affine charts: two distinct points either have an open containing only one, or both lie in one affine open and distinct prime ideals are distinguished by a principal open. Quasi-compactness now gives finitely many such sections $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A$ with affine $Y_{f_i}$ covering $Y$. If $Y$ is empty it is $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$ and the conclusion follows immediately, so in the remaining argument choose $m>0$.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.1, printed p.506, passage from closed-point neighbourhoods to a finite affine principal-open covering; Topology Tag 005E (lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point). Local PDF WANTED; journal PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text:
Consider the map of quasi-coherent polynomial algebra sheaves $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y[T_1,\ldots,T_m]	o\mathcal O_Y[x]$ defined by $T_i\mapsto f_i x$. These algebras are the symmetric algebras of the corresponding finite free modules. On $Y_{f_i}$ the image contains $x$ because $f_i$ is a unit, so $\alpha$ is surjective as a sheaf. Global sections of these polynomial sheaves are $A[T_1,\ldots,T_m]$ and $A[x]$: their underlying modules are direct sums of copies of $\mathcal O_Y$ indexed by monomials, and the degree-zero case of the cited coproduct-cohomology lemma commutes these sums with $\Gamma$. The free-module symmetric-algebra identification makes these identifications multiplicative and sends each variable to the same variable. Apply positive-power lifting to $x$. There are $L>0$ and $g\in A[T_1,\ldots,T_m]$ with $g(f_1x,\ldots,f_mx)=x^L$. Writing $g=\sum_
u a_
u T^
u$, comparison of the coefficient of $x^L$ gives $1=\sum_{|
u|=L}a_
u\prod_i f_i^{
u_i}$. Each term belongs to $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ because $L>0$. Thus this ideal is the unit ideal.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.1, printed p.506, polynomial-algebra surjection and comparison of degree-N coefficients. Local PDF WANTED; journal PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: The finite family $f_i$ generates the unit ideal in $A$ and all $Y_{f_i}$ are affine, so the cited unit-ideal principal-open criterion makes $Y$ affine. Apply Chevalley affineness descent for algebraic spaces to the finite surjective morphism $p:Y\to Z$. It gives that $Z$ is represented by an affine scheme. Every preceding step allowed arbitrary commutative rings and used neither Noetherianity nor finite type of $Z$ over $R$.
